label: Field
definition: The active, moment-to-moment configuration of your active priors, bodily state, context, attention, targets, and available actions. It works as a deep, mobile frame that constantly reconfigures what is relevant to the mind-body-environment system.

label: Target
definition: The currently prioritized preferred outcome of a situation. Action policies are selected partly by how well they are expected to reach it.

label: Prior
definition: A probability distribution stored within a generative model. The field is what priors become when that model is instantiated in a moment of time.

label: Input
definition: Both raw sensory experience, such as seeing or hearing, and the things that experience is organized into, like a dog, a cat, or a mathematical object.

label: Gestalt
definition: The unified whole that appears in the present moment when priors are organized and glued together; the experiential result we perceive.

label: Compression
definition: Preserving contextually important structure while leaving other characteristics out.

label: Layer
definition: One of three stacked layers of knowledge: the embodied layer at the bottom, the representational layer in the middle, and the notational layer, like writing, at the top.

label: Embodied layer
definition: The bottom of the stack: knowledge that lives in the body below immediate conscious awareness, such as gut feelings and tacit knowledge.

label: Representational layer
definition: The middle of the stack: images, simulations, metaphors, concepts, and models that can be internally inspected or manipulated through mental activity, whether implicit or explicit.

label: Notational layer
definition: The top of the stack: external forms, such as writing, diagrams, equations, and labels, that can be stabilized and shared.

label: Notation
definition: External forms, such as writing, diagrams, equations, and labels, that can be stabilized and shared; the contents of the notational layer.

label: Representation
definition: Anything that can be run internally, whether an image, a metaphor, a simulation, or words.

label: Contraction
definition: Tension that participates in maintaining or responding to an active field configuration.

label: Haptic contraction
definition: A felt tightening or clenching in bodily sensation, whether muscular, visceral, or vascular. It is the somatic form a held prior takes in direct experience, whether it is being violated or simply held for use.

label: Latched contraction
definition: Tension that stays stable across situations. Following Michael Johnson, tension that releases in seconds is unlatched, and tension that persists is latched.

label: Friction
definition: A noticeable negative felt response that occurs when an input costs more to integrate than expected.

label: Resonance
definition: A noticeable positive felt response that occurs when an input fits the field and integrates more cheaply than expected.

label: Precision
definition: The weight given to a factor within the field: the estimated reliability or confidence assigned to it, which determines its influence on updating. The essay uses “precision” as shorthand for all forms of precision weighting.

label: Precision weighting
definition: The estimated reliability or confidence assigned to priors or sensory evidence, which then determines their influence on updating.

label: Valence
definition: Whether an experience feels positive, negative, or neutral; a narrow measurement of the felt tone of experience.

label: Slack
definition: Capacity not currently committed to holding the active field configuration in place.

label: Dependency tree
definition: The structure that makes the field’s current configuration possible, with deep, foundational priors at the trunk and more specific interpretations branching out.

label: Chunking
definition: Grouping many separate prior structures into a single unit, such as “water bottle,” so the system can treat the package as one thing rather than evaluating each part separately.

label: Constraint
definition: The binding rules or limits that shape what can fit within the field.

label: Variable
definition: The parts of the field that can change and alter the prediction of the system.

label: Bow tie
definition: The shape of the system’s architecture: one side starts wide, converges into a narrow middle point, then expands back into a wide funnel. The field sits at the narrow point of maximum compression that all input must pass through.

label: Felt sense
definition: Gendlin’s term for a vague, holistic bodily sense of a situation; not just an emotion.

label: Field configuration
definition: The particular arrangement the field takes in a given moment, emergent from conditions like active priors, context, and bodily state.

label: Intuition
definition: Your priors, your implicit structure, speaking directly: the field generating a salient representation or feeling before any explicit derivation.

label: Transparency
definition: The degree to which the processes producing a gestalt remain apparent in experience, on all three layers of the compression gradient, while the gestalt is still being experienced and used.

label: Deep prior
definition: A high-level, foundational prior that sits at the trunk of the dependency tree, with more specific interpretations branching out from it.

label: Inference
definition: The process of moving from the most decompressed input to the most compressed; distributed, hierarchical inference on the input side of the bow tie.

label: Active inference
definition: A process in which the system takes action to make input match its model.

label: Attractor
definition: A configuration the system repeatedly settles into because its components reinforce one another, whether or not the system consciously prefers it.

label: Basin
definition: The range of states from which the system still returns to the same attractor.

label: Reachability
definition: Whether a viable path to an attractor exists under the field’s currently available actions.

label: Craving
definition: The direction of taṇhā in which the target is something like “I need to reach or maintain that state,” so the mind-body system attempts to obtain it.

label: Aversion
definition: The direction of taṇhā in which the target is something like “this state should not be happening,” so the mind-body system attempts to evade the current state.

label: Instantiation
definition: Actively reproducing a persistent prior in the field so it is present in a given context; deep priors are re-instantiated moment to moment.

label: Ontological authority
definition: The degree to which the field builds further inference on a gestalt once it has emerged, like how many priors depend on it.

label: Invariant
definition: Organization that remains stable across a change of input.

label: Action policy
definition: A possible action sequence, selected partly by how well it is expected to reach the target.

label: Cognitive light cone
definition: From Michael Levin: “the scale of the largest goal, in both space and time, which a system is capable of working towards.”

label: Substrate
definition: What the field is instantiated from: the priors, the dependency tree, and their weights.

label: Loop of refinement
definition: The confrontation of intuition with language and logic, through which it is developed and solidified.

label: Open loop
definition: A loop that introduces information or constraints from outside the current model, like working with a tutor to learn a subject.

label: Closed loop
definition: A loop that tests a representation using properties already available within the system, like thinking about an idea on a walk by yourself.

label: Stance
definition: Michael Johnson’s term for recurring patterns of muscular and vascular tension; here, the characteristic somatic patterns that come with field configurations.

label: Target error
definition: The gap between the system’s current and preferred state.

label: Truth-making
definition: The process of testing and updating a model so that it better corresponds with reality.

label: Real-making
definition: The process by which something becomes embodied and actionable within the field.

label: Equanimity
definition: Leaving targets and actions available while making them less compulsory.

label: Sensory clarity
definition: Learning to distinguish phenomena in experience without immediately becoming lost in their movement or story.

label: Emptiness
definition: The negative space of the model: not another component among the others, but a way of seeing the core components from the other side.

label: Compression gradient
definition: The way knowledge moves across the three layers, compressing upward toward notation and decompressing downward toward the body.

label: Interoception
definition: “The process by which the nervous system senses, interprets, and integrates signals originating from within the body, providing a moment-by-moment mapping of the body's internal landscape across conscious and unconscious levels.”

label: Prediction error
definition: The gap between expected input and actual input.

label: Integration cost
definition: How much of the system’s limited capacity an input demands to be integrated, meaning how much the field must reconfigure so the input is accounted for.

label: Tacit knowledge
definition: The actionable expression of intuitions that have been conditioned substantially, as in the knowledge of expertise.

label: Objectification
definition: Making your current model into a stable object you can inspect and manipulate, as when presenting a probe.

label: Field dissonance
definition: When conflicting properties or action policies remain active within the current field while the system must still settle on a workable organization or action.

label: Taṇhā
definition: Literally “thirst,” conventionally translated as craving: the “grabby” or “pushy” thing that interacts with sensations of experience and precedes suffering.

label: First-order hurt
definition: The immediate negatively felt aspect of an experience, registered before the field produces a target that it needs to be different.

label: Thing-ness
definition: A deep prior for objecthood that sits at the trunk of the dependency tree.

label: Suffering loop
definition: The loop that begins when a demand becomes a highly weighted need that present experience must be different, while the preferred state remains difficult to reach.

label: Maintenance loop
definition: The recursive coupling of hurt and taṇhā that keeps the field organized around the target and produces cascading suffering.

label: Energetic triad
definition: The three outcomes of integrating input: cheaper than predicted (positive valence and resonance), about as expected (the neutral fit-baseline), or more costly than predicted (negative valence and friction).

label: Fit-baseline
definition: Where the trunk of the dependency tree structures incoming input without major surprises in either direction; what differences are compared against.

label: De-chunking
definition: Breaking a gestalt back into its parts, as when sensory clarity lets experience appear as changing sensations and events rather than one continuous thing.

label: Structure-preserving transformation
definition: Separating the deeper properties of something, like a fantasy, from its original form and finding new representations or actions that preserve the same properties.

label: Fit distance
definition: Whether input feels closer to or farther from the field’s properties, like a puzzle piece fitting into place.

label: Vasocomputation
definition: Michael Edward Johnson’s hypothesis that active-inference predictions may be physically instantiated through vascular tension.

label: Symmetry Theory of Valence
definition: A theory in which symmetry, one property of the mathematical representation of consciousness, corresponds to how pleasant an experience is.

label: Felt shift
definition: Gendlin’s term for what happens when you find a word, image, or sentence (a handle) that fits the felt sense, and something in you changes physically or emotionally.

label: Structural threshold
definition: A critical point where enough lower-level chunks become sufficiently stable to abruptly percolate into an available higher-order gestalt.

label: Annealing
definition: Temporarily adding energy to a field configuration’s substrate so it can climb out of a basin it is stuck in, explore, and settle into a new configuration.

label: Hysteresis
definition: A form of path dependence in which entering a state and exiting it are asymmetric.

label: Allostasis
definition: The body’s proactive regulation of its own resources.

label: Markov blanket
definition: A boundary of channels: what can cross between the system and the world.

label: Compression progress
definition: The rate at which integration cost is reduced relative to a target.

label: Proxy gestalt
definition: An approximation of a gestalt built from existing structural dependencies, before the priors needed for the actual organization have been established.
